subject.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit

question: Should non-interactive gateway stop permanently require an explicit --force across supported automation, with all owned scripts migrated in the same change?
rationale: This is a deliberate CLI compatibility and operator-safety contract change; code review can identify broken callers but cannot choose the permanent automation policy.

options.title: Adopt guarded automation
options.body: Keep the force-only non-interactive policy, update all owned lifecycle automation, and prove the revised contract end to end.

options.title: Preserve automation compatibility
options.body: Keep existing non-interactive stop behavior and introduce an explicit stricter mode only if maintainers want it as an opt-in contract.

options.title: Pause for lifecycle policy design
options.body: Defer the broad guard until supported release, system-agent, and operator workflows share a reviewed lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded automation
recommendation.body: Keep the force-only non-interactive policy, update all owned lifecycle automation, and prove the revised contract end to end.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and are assigned to the lifecycle-policy series.
